thread:
marta: Nightly eval alert — failing tool/function-call schema on redwood-quant-v2 q8_0 run. Looks like the model is emitting `args` as null or as an object instead of an array. Failing prompts are in tools/lookup set.

marta: Sample model output from the nightly job: 
```json
{"id": "run-2026-04-02-01","tool_calls": [{"name": "lookup","args": null,"raw": "CALL lookup q=\"status\""}]}
```

marta: Expected shape is `tool_calls[].args` === array of positional args or empty array. This breaks the function-calling schema check in the eval harness and downstream tool runners.

samir: Is this only on q8_0 quant or does fp16/different quant levels show same?

marta: Quick glance: fp16 and q4f16 runs are fine. q8_0 is where 90% of these failures come from. Repro on my laptop with the same model artifact reproduces it.

max: Interesting. Could be a decoding/kernel path that collapses list tokens into a single object token during streaming. Any recent kernel/compilation changes on q8?

marta: @samir pushed a small kernel reorder yesterday (deploy 2026-04-01 build 4892). Nightly runs used that. Logs attached below show the model emitted `NULL` token sequence for brackets in some calls.

marta: Repro command I used:
```bash
python evals/run_toolcall_eval.py --model redwood-quant-v2-q8_0 --prompts tools/lookup.jsonl --limit 50 --seed 42 --streaming false
```

max: Can you paste the eval harness output for one bad example (complete generated text)? We need to see whether it's a generation tokenization issue vs post-processor bug.

marta: Pasted full generation (sanitized):
```text
User: lookup status
Model: {"tool_calls": [{"name":"lookup","args": null}]}
```

marta: Post-processor throws: `TypeError: expected list for args, got NoneType`.

samir: Two quick mitigation ideas: 1) Eval harness: accept `null` and coerce to [] with a warning so nightly doesn't explode. 2) Add an input-level assertion to the serving runtime to ensure function-call syntax tokens are emitted as bracketed list. But we should avoid masking a real model regression long-term.

karen: If it's tied to build 4892, can we rollback that kernel for the nightly fleet until we triage? We should limit widespread user impact.

ci-bot: build 4892 was rolled to canary and nightly only. No prod customer endpoints. (build_id: 4892, sha: b3c9f1a) :white_check_mark:

max: Good, reduces blast radius. Still need to track root cause. @marta can you open a bug with minimal repro, attach model artifact hash and the exact tokens around the call? Add `--log-tokens` output.

marta: Done — issue #ML-1489 created with reproducer and artifacts. I included token-level dump.

samir: I'll try local bisect of the kernel reorder and a tiny replay harness. If I can trigger locally I'll push a patch to re-add bracket emit behavior.

max: For short term, let's update nightly eval harness to coerce `null` to [] and emit a regression alert rather than failing the whole run. On the infra side we should record count of coercions so we can spot frequency.

marta: Created PR in evals: fix-coerce-null-args and a monitoring rule to count coercions. Will request review.

karen: Keep me posted. If we see any user-facing rollouts touching q8_0, hold.

nightly-eval-bot: Job 2026-04-02-03:00 completed with 14/50 tool-call items coerced due to null args. See MR: https://git.internal/r/evals/pull/432

ci-bot: CI run for PR fix-coerce-null-args passed unit + integration tests (run-1728004).

max: Thanks team. After patch lands, rerun the nightly on q8_0 and compare token-level diffs. If coercions drop to zero, we can mark as mitigated. Root cause triage continues. :mag:
